evals.prompt: Create a new operations dashboard from scratch. I have not chosen a visual style, so let me review the direction before you implement it.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces a compact design brief, recommends or opens appropriate dashboard previews, waits for selection, and treats title, metadata, favicon, responsiveness, and component states as part of the eventual implementation.
assertions: Classifies the request as a new page and uses the undecided preview-selection path.
Does not implement the final page before the user selects a direction.
Includes the new-project shell and favicon.ico in the implementation requirements.
Chooses an operational dashboard archetype rather than a marketing hero layout.

evals.prompt: Add an approval queue page to this existing legacy admin frontend. Match the rest of the product and do not redesign unrelated screens.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects nearby routes, sibling list pages, wrappers, tokens, table and feedback patterns before coding, then implements the smallest compatible feature without forcing style selection.
assertions: Classifies the work as an existing-project feature.
Inspects real nearby frontend code and shared components before implementation.
Reuses table, button, pagination, filter, overlay, icon, and feedback conventions where present.
Does not open the preview gallery unless the existing design system is a blocker.

evals.prompt: Polish only the delete-confirmation modal in this settings page. Keep the surrounding page unchanged.
evals.expected_output: The agent defines the target and neighbor boundaries, preserves project tokens and overlay anatomy, and verifies focus entry and return, Escape, close behavior, loading, errors, scrolling, and mobile fallback.
assertions: Uses local UI patch mode and the modal/drawer/confirmation pattern.
Does not redesign the full settings page.
Covers visible close, focus management, Escape, destructive wording, and async protection.
Checks desktop and mobile overlay behavior.

evals.prompt: This save button currently calls window.alert for success and window.confirm before overwrite. Replace those interactions with finished product UI.
evals.expected_output: The agent replaces success alerts with project feedback and overwrite confirmation with a project modal, drawer, inline decision, or reliable undo pattern, then scans changed files for browser-dialog primitives.
assertions: Rejects window.alert and window.confirm as finished product UI.
Maps success feedback and blocking confirmation to patterns with the correct scope.
Includes accessibility, error, loading, and recovery behavior.
Runs or requests the UI primitive anti-pattern scan.

evals.prompt: Build a small new static form with a single short country selector. There is no UI library and it does not need search or rich options.
evals.expected_output: The agent may use a deliberately styled native select for this simple new-project case, while providing a label, focus-visible state, validation, disabled behavior, long-value handling, and a non-default visual treatment.
assertions: Distinguishes a simple selection from complex combobox behavior.
Does not build an unnecessary custom combobox or add a dependency.
Does not ship an unstyled browser-default control.
Preserves native semantics and keyboard behavior.

evals.prompt: Add an async searchable multi-select with grouped results to an existing project that already wraps an accessible combobox library.
evals.expected_output: The agent reuses the existing wrapper and option model, covers loading, empty, error, selected and disabled states, and verifies active-option semantics, keyboard navigation, overlay placement, and mobile behavior.
assertions: Chooses the existing accessible wrapper before native or custom implementations.
Covers async, grouped, multi-select, long-value, and failure states.
Verifies combobox/listbox semantics and keyboard behavior.
Avoids adding another select library.

evals.prompt: Implement a paginated results table with filters, sorting, row selection, bulk actions, row menus, and mobile support inside our current web app.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows the existing table and query-state contract, implements all data states and selection semantics, and chooses a deliberate mobile fallback rather than compressing the desktop table until it is unreadable.
assertions: Inspects and reuses the project table, pagination, filter, permission, and formatting patterns.
Covers loading, empty, filtered-empty, error, stale, selection, and pagination states.
Clarifies page-only versus all-results selection.
Tests first, middle, last, page-size, and delete-last-row behavior.

evals.prompt: Repair this existing responsive page: at 390px the chips and primary button overlap the headline, while desktop already looks correct.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the change as a local mobile repair, inspects the current layout, moves conflicting controls into stable flow or constrained regions, and verifies text fit and controls at 390px plus a narrower stress width.
assertions: Preserves the desktop visual direction and unrelated regions.
Removes overlap instead of merely hiding important content.
Uses stable responsive constraints and normal flow where appropriate.
Verifies horizontal overflow, text fit, and reachable controls on mobile.

evals.prompt: Design and build a new product page. Pick the most suitable style yourself and proceed without asking me to approve the choice.
evals.expected_output: The agent selects a suitable style, states the choice and concise reasoning, sets the layout archetype and design dials, then proceeds directly while still completing shell, responsive, primitive, and verification requirements.
assertions: Uses the delegated direct-implementation branch of the preview gate.
Does not add an unnecessary confirmation pause.
Names the selected direction and explains why it fits the page job.
Still applies new-project shell and implementation-compliance checks.

evals.prompt: Review these frontend files for UI implementation compliance. Focus on native controls, browser dialogs, accessibility, responsive text, loading and error recovery, and consistency with nearby pages.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports concrete findings by severity and file or region, compares nearby project patterns, scans for banned primitives, and identifies state, accessibility, and responsive gaps without forcing a visual redesign.
assertions: Uses implementation-compliance mode and leads with findings.
Checks browser dialogs, native selects, focus visibility, semantics, text fit, and reduced motion.
Checks loading, empty, error, retry, disabled, and permission states where relevant.
Reports verification scope, remaining exceptions, and test gaps.
